title: SessionStart gh probe may run a gh.exe planted in the opened project directory (Windows)
description: On every SessionStart (startup, resume, clear, compact), the hook calls spawnSync('gh.exe', ['--version'], {shell:false}). It passes a bare name and sets no cwd, so the child inherits the project directory as its cwd. If the Windows process-spawn path in Node/libuv searches the current directory before PATH, a cloned third-party repository containing gh.exe at the opened directory runs that binary as the user. This happens automatically on session start, with no agent tool call and no host tool-permission prompt.
claimed_root_cause: probeGitHubCli resolves the executable by bare name. It relies on shell:false as its only control and sets no explicit trusted cwd, no absolute path and no PATH filtering. Executable search order is left to the platform's runtime, while the cwd is the lower-trust project directory.

trace.description: Host runs node stilo-activate.js on startup|resume|clear|compact (matcher at line 5), with the session's working directory.
Calls probeGitHubCli() unconditionally, with the process cwd being the opened project.
spawnSync('gh.exe',['--version'],{timeout:1000,shell:false,windowsHide:true}): bare name, no cwd option, inherited env; process creation is the sink.

evidence.description: Bare-name gh.exe spawn without cwd or absolute path; shell:false is the only control.
Hook operates on process.cwd(), which is the project directory (docs/contrato-hooks.md:41 states the hook runs with the session cwd).
Matcher startup|resume|clear|compact makes the probe run at every session start and context reset.

blockers: Not observable without execution (no OS sandbox on this host): whether Node 24.19.0 / libuv uv_spawn on Windows, with shell:false and a bare file name such as 'gh.exe', searches the child's cwd before PATH, and whether it honors NoDefaultCurrentDirectoryInExePath.

Host fact: whether Claude Code and Codex start SessionStart plugin hooks with the opened project directory as process cwd, and whether a workspace-trust prompt precedes plugin hooks. If trust already permits repo-defined hooks (for example .claude/settings.json), the boundary crossed is smaller, though the planted file is stealthier and plugin-scoped.

validation_plan.local: In a disposable Windows VM with Node 24.19.0 and gh not installed or on PATH, create an empty directory containing a copy of a benign system binary renamed gh.exe (for example hostname.exe). From that directory, run a minimal harness: node -e "const r=require('child_process').spawnSync('gh.exe',['--version'],{shell:false,encoding:'utf8'});console.log(r.error&&r.error.code,r.stdout)". If stdout shows the hostname instead of ENOENT, the cwd copy was executed. Repeat with NoDefaultCurrentDirectoryInExePath=1 set.
validation_plan.deployment: The owner observes in Claude Code and in Codex on Windows, opening a dummy project folder, which process cwd the SessionStart hook receives (for example by temporarily logging process.cwd() from a local copy of the plugin) and whether a folder-trust prompt is shown before plugin hooks run.

title: Agent-run GitHub CLI installer may run a project-planted winget.exe or gh.exe (Windows)
description: When the probe reports gh absent, the SessionStart note tells the agent to run node <pluginRoot>/scripts/setup-github-cli.js. The script's realRun spawns bare names ('gh.exe', then 'winget.exe') with shell:false, inherited env and no cwd, so they run in the agent's working directory, normally the project. A repository that plants winget.exe (but not gh.exe, which keeps the probe at 'absent' and makes the setup note appear) would have its binary launched as the user if Windows executable search includes the current directory first. The host tool-permission prompt shows only 'node .../setup-github-cli.js', not the binary that is actually resolved.
claimed_root_cause: realRun resolves installer and probe executables by bare name and inherits the caller's cwd. There is no absolute path resolution (for example a PATH lookup that excludes cwd, or a fixed System32/WindowsApps path for winget) and no explicit trusted cwd. Only the knownWindowsExecutable fallback is absolute.

trace.description: The SessionStart context tells the agent to execute node with the setup-github-cli.js path when the probe status is 'absent'.
First invoke('gh.exe',['--version']). On ENOENT, the script continues to the install path.
On win32, manager='winget.exe' (bare name).
invoke(manager,['--version']), then invoke(manager,args,180000) at line 91.
spawn(file,args,{shell:false,windowsHide:true,stdio:[...],env:{...process.env,...}}) with no cwd option: process creation resolved from the inherited cwd and PATH.

evidence.description: spawn without cwd option and with a bare file name passed by callers.
winget.exe referenced by bare name.
Only knownWindowsExecutable uses an absolute path, which shows the sibling control is not applied to winget.exe or gh.exe.
The setup note is emitted only when the probe status is 'absent' (gh ENOENT, no lock or receipt), which is the precondition an attacker gets by planting winget.exe without gh.exe.

blockers: Not observable without execution (no OS sandbox on this host): whether Node 24.19.0 / libuv on Windows searches the current directory before PATH for bare names such as 'winget.exe' with shell:false.

Host or agent fact: which cwd the AI agent uses when it runs the setup script (the project directory is expected but depends on the agent's Bash or PowerShell tool), and whether the host permission prompt is shown and approved for that command.

validation_plan.local: In a disposable Windows VM with Node 24.19.0, no gh, and a benign binary renamed winget.exe (for example hostname.exe) in an otherwise empty directory, run from that directory: node -e "require('child_process').spawn('winget.exe',['--version'],{shell:false,stdio:['ignore','pipe','pipe']}).stdout.on('data',d=>console.log(String(d)))". Output from the renamed binary instead of the system winget confirms cwd-first resolution. Do not run the real installer.
validation_plan.deployment: The owner observes, in a dummy project in Claude Code and in Codex on Windows, the working directory the agent uses when it follows the setup note (for example by running a local copy of the script that prints process.cwd() and exits).

title: Project discovery walks above the user's/repository's boundary, letting a state.json in a shared ancestor directory (e.g. C:\.stilo) become the active project
description: findStateFiles climbs from the hook cwd to the filesystem root with no ceiling, ownership or home/repo boundary and accepts the first <ancestor>/.stilo/state.json it finds. On hosts where a different, lower-privileged principal can create a directory in an ancestor of the victim's working directory (default Windows ACLs allow Authenticated Users to create folders in C:\, the same condition behind git's CVE-2022-24765 ceiling fix; also /tmp-style shared dirs, UNC/share roots), that principal can plant .stilo/state.json and .stilo/checkpoint.json. Every SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit and SubagentStart for any victim session without a nearer state file then resolves that planted file as the project: its project/updated/checkpoint task/nextAction/pending text is injected into the agent's context under the protected '## Estado do Stilo Code' block, its phase selects which modules and next action the agent receives (e.g. EXECUTE -> 'seguir plan.md na ordem'), and AGENTS.md:99 tells the agent to write subsequent phase transitions back to that attacker-readable path. Alternatively a malformed or directory-typed planted state.json forces the 'state.json ilegÃ­vel ... nÃ£o crie nem reinicie o projeto' / 'nÃ£o avance nem aja' directives for every such victim session, suppressing the normal 'no project -> create one' flow.
claimed_root_cause: hooks/stilo-state.js#findStateFiles loops `for (;;) { if (fs.existsSync(candidato(atual))) return [p]; const pai = path.dirname(atual); if (pai === atual) break; atual = pai; }` with no stop at a trust boundary (user home, repository root, configured ceiling) and no check that the found .stilo directory/state.json is owned by the current user, so ownership of the active project is decided by whichever ancestor directory first contains .stilo/state.json.

trace.description: resolveProjeto(process.cwd()) on every session start (SubagentStart: hooks/stilo-subagent.js:8; UserPromptSubmit: hooks/stilo-prompt.js:19 with host data.cwd).
Calls findStateFiles(cwd); a single hit becomes statePath and is read/validated (:283-293).
Unbounded upward loop: returns the first ancestor .stilo/state.json (:87) and only stops when path.dirname reaches the root (:91-92).
The ancestor's sibling .stilo/checkpoint.json is derived from the selected statePath and read by buildCheckpointNote (:72), rendering task, nextAction ('prÃ³xima:') and pending (:85-87).

Planted phase selects PROXIMA_ACAO/MODELO_ALVO and modules (modulosDaFase :159-166); project and updated rendered (:271,285); unreadable/invalid planted files instead emit 'do not create/act' directives (:206-238).
The assembled context is written to stdout and consumed by the host as agent context (SubagentStart/Codex via envelope at :33,:38).

evidence.description: findStateFiles has no ceiling/home/repo-root parameter or ownership check; comment at :70 states it mirrors git's upward search.
The only termination condition is reaching the filesystem root (pai === atual).
Ruleset instructs the same unbounded upward search, so the agent's own lookup shares the flaw.
Agent is told to write phase transitions to the found state.json, i.e. into the planted ancestor location.
An unreadable planted state.json yields 'nÃ£o crie nem reinicie o projeto; corrija o arquivo antes de agir' in every prompt line.
Tests cover only in-tree upward precedence; no test asserts a boundary above the workspace/home.

blockers: Whether a principal other than the session user can create <ancestor>/.stilo/state.json above a typical working directory is an OS/ACL fact (e.g. default 'Authenticated Users: Create folders' on C:\, sticky /tmp, network share roots) that is not source-visible.

The hook cannot be executed in this run: no OS-enforced sandbox is available on the host, so the end-to-end injection of a planted ancestor state into SessionStart/UserPromptSubmit output was not observed.
How the host (Claude Code / Codex) and the model treat the injected state block is runtime behavior outside source.

validation_plan.local: Inside an approved sandbox with a throwaway root: create <root>/.stilo/state.json = {"version":1,"project":"PLANTED","phase":"EXECUTE","reviewRound":0} and <root>/.stilo/checkpoint.json with nextAction 'PLANTED-NEXT', create <root>/u/victim/proj with no .stilo, then call require('hooks/stilo-state.js').resolveProjeto('<root>/u/victim/proj') and require('hooks/stilo-instructions.js').buildInjectedContext(r.state, r.caminhos). Expected if vulnerable: statePath is <root>/.stilo/state.json and the output contains 'Projeto:** PLANTED', 'Fase:** EXECUTE' and 'prÃ³xima: PLANTED-NEXT'. Repeat with state.json as a directory to observe the 'ilegÃ­vel ... nÃ£o crie' directive. Regression: with a ceiling at the user home/repo root (or an owner check), the same call must return status 'absent'.
validation_plan.deployment: Owner-observed on a Windows host: run `icacls C:\` and confirm whether 'NT AUTHORITY\Authenticated Users' has '(AD)' / create-folder rights on the drive root; as a second local standard account, check whether `mkdir C:\.stilo` succeeds. On POSIX, check whether common working-directory ancestors (/tmp, shared mounts) are writable by other users.

title: Repository-authored checkpoint/state text is auto-injected as plugin-authored 'prÃ³xima:' state with no provenance label
description: The SessionStart, SubagentStart and UserPromptSubmit hooks read .stilo/checkpoint.json and .stilo/state.json from the resolved project directory. That directory can be a third-party clone, or a single subfolder of the opened workspace. The hooks inject the free-text fields (checkpoint task, nextAction, pending; state project) into the agent's context inside the protected '## Estado do Stilo Code' plugin block. Checkpoint nextAction is rendered as 'prÃ³xima: <text>' right after the plugin's own 'PrÃ³xima aÃ§Ã£o'. The only neutralization is whitespace collapse plus truncation, so no deterministic control marks this text as repository data rather than plugin instruction. The agent receives it without choosing to read the file, through hook context. Any resulting action would run under the user's tool authority, gated only by the host permission prompt. In the in-repository layout, the repository author probably already has an equal or stronger channel through host-loaded CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md, which would mean no marginal boundary crossing. The decisive questions are host instruction-file loading for the layouts where this text is injected (notably the one-level-down discovery) and model obedience to the framing. Neither is source-visible or locally observable without execution.
claimed_root_cause: stilo-instructions.js presents repository-controlled free text (checkpoint.nextAction/task/pending, state.project) as plugin state. The only treatment is sanitiza, which collapses whitespace and truncates, with no provenance label, quoting or data framing. In particular checkpoint.nextAction is rendered as an imperative 'prÃ³xima:' line inside a protected plugin block. validateCheckpoint enforces only types and non-emptiness.

For a valid state, calls buildCheckpointNote(caminhos.statePath, false), which reads <statePath dir>/checkpoint.json
Accepts any non-empty strings for task and nextAction and any string array for pending. No content constraint

'## Estado do Stilo Code' is a protected marker, so the block that carries the repository text is always kept
Writes the context to hook stdout. The host adds it to the agent's model context (Claude Code SessionStart raw stdout; SubagentStart envelope at line 38; Codex JSON at line 33)

If they do (as is likely in the in-repository layout), the attacker gains no capability and the candidate is refuted for that layout. The one-level-down layout is the decisive one.

title: SessionStart/SubagentStart hooks read a repo-controlled .stilo/checkpoint.json without refusing symlinks, special files or large sizes
description: In a cloned repository with a valid .stilo/state.json, the SessionStart and SubagentStart hooks read the sibling .stilo/checkpoint.json with fs.readFileSync. They do not lstat it, require a regular file, refuse a symlink, or cap its size. On POSIX, git checks out a committed symlink such as .stilo/checkpoint.json -> /dev/zero (or a very large regular file). The hook would then try to buffer an endless or huge stream into memory until the host's 5 s timeout kills it. That would cost the user's machine a transient multi-GB memory spike at every session start and every subagent start, and silently drop the plugin's injected context. The impact is availability of the user's own workstation and of the plugin guidance. The size of the effect cannot be confirmed without execution.
claimed_root_cause: readJsonObject (hooks/stilo-state.js:202-209), used by readCheckpoint, passes a path taken from repo-controlled discovery straight to fs.readFileSync(filePath,'utf8'). There is no lstat/O_NOFOLLOW, no isFile() check and no byte limit. The only bound is the external 5 s hook timeout.

trace.description: resolveProjeto(process.cwd()) discovers <project>/.stilo/state.json in the opened (possibly third-party) clone; stilo-subagent.js:9 does the same on SubagentStart
Called from buildInjectedContext (line 316), it builds the state block via blocoEstado(state, caminhos)
For a valid state, calls buildCheckpointNote(caminhos.statePath, false)
Derives path.join(dirname(statePath),'checkpoint.json'), a repo-controlled filename that may be a committed symlink
Delegates to readJsonObject with no file-type or size precheck
fs.readFileSync(filePath,'utf8') follows symlinks and reads until EOF; for a device like /dev/zero there is no EOF

evidence.description: Unbounded readFileSync of the checkpoint path; the only guard is try/catch returning null
Checkpoint read happens on every SessionStart/SubagentStart context build when state.json is valid
Host timeout of 5 s is the only bound on the read (also line 37 for SubagentStart)
Code comment acknowledges .stilo content may come from a cloned repository (lower-trust input), but the control is only text sanitization, not file-type/size validation
Sibling code in the same repo refuses symlinks and special files via lstat, which shows the missing equivalent control in the hook readers

How fast Node >=20 fs.readFileSync grows memory on a non-regular (size 0) file, and its hard limit before throwing, is runtime behavior not visible in source
Whether Claude Code / Codex enforce the 5 s timeout by killing the hook process (and how long memory stays allocated) is host behavior outside source
Whether git checkout on the user's platform materializes the absolute symlink (core.symlinks default true on POSIX, false on Windows) is an environment fact

title: Per-prompt state.json read follows a repository-planted symlink to a device or FIFO, with no file-type or size check
description: A cloned or extracted project can ship `.stilo/state.json` as a symlink to /dev/zero (git stores symlinks and materializes them by default on Linux/macOS) or as a FIFO (via archive extraction). On every UserPromptSubmit, SessionStart and SubagentStart, resolveProjeto â†’ readStateResult synchronously calls fs.readFileSync(statePath,'utf8') on it. For /dev/zero the read never reaches EOF and the buffer keeps growing. For a FIFO it blocks. In both cases the hook runs until the host's 5 s timeout kills it, the Stilo state injection is lost, and each prompt is delayed. For /dev/zero, memory may also spike by multiple GB on the developer's machine. Concurrent SubagentStart hooks multiply that. If timeout kill reaches only the shell parent, an orphaned node could keep allocating until the system runs out of memory. The trigger persists in the repository until the user removes it. This is a sibling of the checkpoint candidate hooks/stilo-state.js:readJsonObject:unbounded-readFileSync-checkpoint-special-file, but it is a different function on the per-prompt path and needs its own fix.
claimed_root_cause: hooks/stilo-state.js#readStateResult passes a path taken from repository-controlled discovery (findStateFiles, which only checks fs.existsSync and so follows symlinks) straight to fs.readFileSync(statePath,'utf8'). There is no lstat or no-follow open, no isFile() check and no byte cap. Unlike the unwired sibling stilo-diagnostics.js#fileCheck, it never verifies the target is a regular file. The only bound is the external host hook timeout, because the prompt hook's own 1 s timer cannot fire while the synchronous read blocks the event loop.

trace.description: UserPromptSubmit hook resolves the project for the host-supplied cwd on every user prompt (SessionStart stilo-activate.js:9 and SubagentStart stilo-subagent.js:8 do the same with process.cwd()).
fs.existsSync(<dir>/.stilo/state.json) follows symlinks and accepts any existing target type, including devices and FIFOs.
The single discovered path is passed unchanged to readStateResult.
fs.readFileSync(statePath,'utf8') reads synchronously with no type, link or size check, so it is unbounded on /dev/zero and blocking on a FIFO.

evidence.description: Unconditional readFileSync of the discovered path; the catch at 133-138 only handles thrown errors, not non-terminating reads.
Discovery test is existsSync only, which follows symlinks; no lstat in the module.
Prompt hook self-timeout is an unref'd setTimeout that cannot run while main blocks synchronously inside the 'end' handler.
Only bound is host timeout 5 s per hook; the same applies to SessionStart (line 11) and SubagentStart (line 37).
Sibling reader rejects non-regular files with statSync().isFile(); the wired hook path has no equivalent control.

blockers: No OS-enforced sandbox on this host, so a resolveProjeto call against a /dev/zero symlink or FIFO fixture could not be executed. The Node 24 readFileSync('utf8') behaviour on a character device (readFileUtf8 fast path: growth rate, bad_alloc versus ERR_STRING_TOO_LONG) is unobserved.
Host behaviour at the 5 s hook timeout is not source-visible: whether Claude Code/Codex kill the node process or only the `sh -c` / PowerShell parent, and whether the prompt proceeds.
Peak RSS within the timeout window, and whether concurrent SubagentStart hooks cause system-wide memory pressure, are unobserved.

Materialization of the symlink depends on the git client config (core.symlinks). It defaults to true on Linux/macOS and false on Git for Windows, so the default Windows host is likely not affected by the symlink vector.

validation_plan.local: In an isolated Linux VM or container with networking disabled, an empty environment, the repo mounted read-only, a memory cgroup limit (e.g. 256 MB) and a 6 s wall-clock limit: create fixture dir F with `.stilo/state.json -> /dev/zero`. Run `node -e "require('/ro/stilo-code/hooks/stilo-state.js').resolveProjeto('F')"`, then record whether it is OOM-killed or still running at timeout, and its peak RSS. Repeat with `mkfifo F/.stilo/state.json` and confirm it blocks until the wall limit. Then `git clone` a local bare repo committing that symlink, with default config, and confirm the symlink is materialized.
validation_plan.deployment: Owner check on a Linux or macOS workstation with Claude Code: open a disposable project containing `.stilo/state.json -> /dev/zero`, submit one prompt, and observe in a process monitor whether the hook's node process is terminated at 5 s (no orphan survives its shell parent), its peak RSS, and whether the prompt continues. On Windows, confirm `git config core.symlinks` is false by default, so the symlink is checked out as a plain text file.

title: Injected 'fix/write .stilo/state.json' directives can steer the agent to overwrite a user file outside the project through a repository-planted symlink
description: A third-party repository can ship .stilo/state.json (or the .stilo directory) as a symlink to a file outside the project. Examples are a JSON config such as ~/.claude/settings.json or ~/.docker/config.json, which lands in the 'invalid' branch, or any non-JSON dotfile, which lands in the 'unreadable' branch. Discovery accepts the link because fs.existsSync follows it. The hooks then inject a protected plugin-state block that names the in-project link path as the 'Arquivo'. The block tells the agent, as high-authority plugin instructions, that it must correct all fields of state.json (invalid) or fix the file (unreadable) before doing anything else. Every subsequent prompt repeats 'nÃ£o avance nem aja atÃ© corrigir o arquivo'. The valid branch also tells the agent to write the next phase into .stilo/state.json. If the agent's write tool follows the link, the user's file outside the project is overwritten or edited with Stilo state JSON. The agent's tool-permission system is the only remaining gate.
claimed_root_cause: Neither hooks/stilo-state.js#findStateFiles nor resolveProjeto checks the identity of the discovered state path before blocoEstado/buildStateLine tell the agent to write or repair it. There is no lstat or no-follow check on the .stilo component or the state.json leaf, no realpath containment inside the project directory and no isFile check. Discovery uses only fs.existsSync, which follows links. The injected text then shows the unresolved link path, so the agent and the user cannot see that the write target lies outside the project.

trace.description: resolveProjeto(process.cwd()) runs on the opened, possibly cloned, project directory. stilo-subagent.js:8 and stilo-prompt.js:45 do the same for SubagentStart and UserPromptSubmit.

Candidate <dir>/.stilo/state.json is accepted with fs.existsSync(p), which follows symlinks. A symlinked .stilo directory or state.json leaf whose target exists is returned as the active path, with no lstat or containment check (same at :108 for the one-level scan).

readStateResult(statePath) reads through the link (readFileSync at :132). A non-JSON target gives status 'unreadable' (:285-286). A JSON object missing the state fields gives 'invalid' (:289-291). statePath keeps the lexical link path.
Shows '- **Arquivo:** <link path>' inside the protected '## Estado do Stilo Code' block, the unresolved in-project-looking path.

Directs the agent: 'NÃ£o avance nem aja no projeto atÃ© corrigir todos os campos do `state.json`.' The unreadable branch at :217 says 'Corrija o `state.json` antes de agir.', the valid branch at :290 says 'grave vocÃª mesmo a fase seguinte em `.stilo/state.json`', and buildStateLine at :176/:183 repeats this on every prompt. The agent's file-write tool is the effect sink.

evidence.description: if (fs.existsSync(p)) return [p]; is the only acceptance test for the discovered state path, and it follows symlinks.

The one-level scan rejects symlinked subdirectories through Dirent.isDirectory(), but it never checks the .stilo component or the state.json leaf. This shows the identity check is partial, not absent by design.
readStateResult reads statePath with fs.readFileSync, following links. There is no lstat, isFile or realpath containment check before the status is decided.
Unreadable branch: 'NÃ£o crie nem reinicie o projeto. Corrija o `state.json` antes de agir.' A repair directive for a file whose identity was never checked.
Invalid branch: 'NÃ£o avance nem aja no projeto atÃ© corrigir todos os campos do `state.json`.' A link to any JSON-object file outside the project reaches it.
Valid branch: 'Ao concluir esta fase, grave vocÃª mesmo a fase seguinte em `.stilo/state.json`.'
buildStateLine re-injects 'state.json invÃ¡lido em <link path> ... nÃ£o avance nem aja atÃ© corrigir o arquivo' on every user prompt.
The only file-type check in the codebase (statSync().isFile()) follows links and is not wired into any hook. Even it would accept a symlink to a regular file outside the project.
The injected ruleset makes writing state.json the agent's responsibility at each phase transition, with no symlink or containment precondition.

blockers: Host write-tool behavior is not source-visible. It is unknown whether Claude Code's Write/Edit tools (and Codex's apply_patch/shell writes) follow a symlink at .stilo/state.json or a symlinked .stilo directory. It is also unknown whether their permission check resolves the real target path, so that a target outside the working directory triggers an out-of-workspace prompt or denial, or uses the lexical in-project path and auto-allows the write.

Checkout behavior is a platform fact. git creates tracked symlinks on POSIX clones, but on Windows only with core.symlinks=true and symlink privilege (Developer Mode or admin). The host here is Windows, where a default clone would check the link out as a plain text file. That gives 'unreadable' with no outside-project write.

Agent behavior is not deterministic. Whether the model, after reading the link target's content (which the tool shows), actually writes or edits the file rather than reporting the anomaly needs an owner-observed run.

No OS-enforced sandbox is available on this host, so no hook or target code was executed. Whether a symlinked state.json reaches the 'invalid' or 'unreadable' injected block was established from source only.

title: Injected companion recommendations may lend plugin trust to a project-supplied MCP server with the same name
description: An operator opens an untrusted project containing a project-local MCP server named `context7` or `playwright`. Stilo injects plugin-authored instructions recommending those names as MCP companions and saying to use them when available. If the host loads the project server and the agent treats the name match as endorsement, it may send tool requests or context to the untrusted server. Source confirms the injected recommendation, but does not establish project MCP loading, consent behavior, or whether the agent relies on the recommendation when selecting a server.
claimed_root_cause: The plugin injects bare MCP companion names as trusted recommendations without binding them to an authenticated server identity or distinguishing plugin-provided tools from project-provided tools. Whether this crosses a trust boundary depends on host and agent behavior not established in source.

trace.description: The hook resolves the opened project's state before building the context to inject.
The plugin reads AGENTS.md from pluginRoot and combines it with state and applicable modules.
The injected rules name context7 and playwright as MCP companions and recommend them for project phases.
The assembled instructions are returned to the host as additional context; whether they influence selection of a project-supplied same-name server is host/model behavior.

evidence.description: The rules instruct the agent to use a listed companion if installed and proceed without it otherwise.
context7 is explicitly identified as an MCP companion.
playwright is explicitly identified as an MCP companion.
lerArquivo reads instruction files from pluginRoot; the AGENTS.md text is plugin-authored context.
buildFullContext includes the plugin-root AGENTS.md text in the context assembled for SessionStart and SubagentStart.
SessionStart passes buildInjectedContext output to writeHookOutput.
Context selection operates on text blocks and protected markers; it does not bind a companion name to a server identity.

blockers: Source does not establish whether Claude Code or Codex automatically loads project-local MCP configuration, what user consent or trust gates apply, or whether those controls show the actual server identity.
Source cannot establish whether an agent interprets Stilo's name-only recommendation as endorsement of a same-name project server or sends sensitive tool input to it.

validation_plan.local: In an approved OS-enforced sandbox with networking disabled, use a disposable project and a harmless dummy MCP server named `context7`; configure it to record only a fixed nonsensitive test request. Observe whether the host loads the project configuration, what consent or identity information it presents, and whether the agent treats the injected Stilo recommendation as endorsement. Do not use real credentials or project data. If such a sandbox is unavailable, do not run the target and retain this blocker.
validation_plan.deployment: Owner-observed in a disposable Claude Code and Codex profile: open a throwaway project with a harmless same-name project MCP server and the plugin installed. Record whether the host loads it, whether consent identifies its source and endpoint, and whether the agent selects it because of the injected companion recommendation. Do not use a production project, real credentials, or sensitive prompts.
